summary: Grammar-state MoE (6 experts, k=1 router on a recurrent parse-state slot) reaches dev bpc 0.6829, top1 0.8083 from the 5.0-bpc uniform bootstrap; route counts det 13141, adjn 22200, post 13593, verb 1905, adv 1273, func 2374.

Lowering the relative probability floor from 1e-3 to 1e-6 and re-estimating determiner/modifier probabilities lowered bpc 0.7257 -> 0.6841; max per-position cost stayed <= 6.3 bits, i.e. no dev character violated the hand-written grammar.
A document-length rule (eos after '.' only once step >= 150) cut after_period bpc from 0.044 to 0.007.
Tracking NP modifier depth in state and forbidding modifiers at depth 2 (never seen while reading) gave a small gain (0.6844 -> 0.6838) with no large-surprise positions.

Re-estimating probabilities from a second hand-read batch did not change bpc (0.6841 vs 0.6844); remaining loss is likely close to the source grammar's entropy, so further gains need new structure (e.g. per-document caches) rather than calibration.
